title: HXX2: markup parser + build-macro rewrite
description:
PLAN_REF: plans/active/hxx2-default-authoring-path.md#-1-macro-rewrite-beads-haxeelixir-hxx22

FILES
- src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/InlineMarkup.hx

WHAT
- Make inline markup default-on for Phoenix-facing modules by rewriting `@:markup` into the canonical entrypoint: `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root(<typed template expr>)`.
- Parse `{ ... }` blocks inside inline markup into real Haxe `Expr` nodes using `Context.parseInlineString`, then reconstruct the template as a typed Haxe expression (string fragments + embedded expressions).

ALGORITHM
- Rewrite rule:
  - Before: `@:markup <payload>` -> `HXX.hxx(<payload>)` (legacy string-template path)
  - After:  `@:markup <payload>` -> `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root(<typedExpr>)`
- Payload scanning must be deterministic and quote-aware:
  - Split payload into literal chunks and expression chunks delimited by braces.
  - Track quote state for `"` and `'` so braces inside quoted attribute values do not start expressions.
  - Track brace depth for nested braces inside an expression.
  - Fail fast on: unclosed `{`, stray `}`, empty `{}`.
- Expression parsing:
  - For each expression chunk, call `Context.parseInlineString(exprText, pos)` to produce a typed Haxe `Expr`.
  - Parenthesize parsed expressions when stitching to avoid precedence issues.
- Reconstruction:
  - Build a Haxe AST equivalent to: `"<lit1>" + (expr1) + "<lit2>" + (expr2) + ...`.
  - Fast path: if no expressions exist, call `HeexTemplate.root(<stringConst>)` directly.

DEFAULTS / OPT-OUT / LEGACY
- Default-on for Phoenix-facing modules (same concept as current `shouldProcessLocalType`).
- Global opt-out: `-D hxx_no_inline_markup`.
- Per-class opt-out: `@:hxx_no_inline_markup`.
- Legacy escape hatch: `@:hxx_legacy` forces legacy rewrite to `HXX.hxx(...)` for that class.

FAILURE MODES / DIAGNOSTICS
- Errors must be positional: point at the offending span inside the inline-markup payload.
- Messages must include the fix (correct braces, or opt-out / legacy escape hatch).

TESTS (add fixtures)
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_inline_markup_basic
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_inline_markup_attrs_expr
- Negative: test/snapshot/negative/heex_template_inline_markup_brace_errors

VERIFICATION
- npm test
- npm run qa:sentinel then scripts/qa-logpeek.sh --run-id <RUN_ID> --until-done 120

ROLLOUT
- Keep HXX1 (string templates) working unchanged.
- Enable inline markup rewrite by default only for Phoenix-facing modules; opt-outs available.

NOTES
- Canonical entrypoint is `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1`; `phoenix.hxx.HXX2.root/1` remains as deprecated alias.
acceptance_criteria:
- Inline markup works without -D
- { ... } blocks parsed as Haxe Expr (Context.parseInlineString)
- Errors are positional + fail-fast
- Opt-out exists: -D hxx_no_inline_markup and @:hxx_no_inline_markup
- Legacy escape hatch exists: @:hxx_legacy
close_reason: Completed by commit 7a10c5dc

title: HXX2: builder lowering to ~H
description:
PLAN_REF: plans/active/hxx2-default-authoring-path.md#-2-builder-lowering-beads-haxeelixir-hxx23

FILES
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/builders/CallExprBuilder.hx
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/HeexStringReturnToSigilTransforms.hx

WHAT
- Lower `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1` to `ESigil("H", content, "")` deterministically in the typed AST (same semantics as `HXX.hxx/1`).

ALGORITHM
- In `CallExprBuilder`, detect static calls where:
  - class is `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate` (also accept deprecated alias `phoenix.hxx.HXX2`)
  - method is `root`
  - arity is 1
- Build the argument expression as ElixirAST (`innerAst`).
- Convert to HEEx string:
  - `content = TemplateHelpers.collectTemplateContent(innerAst)`
  - `content = HeexControlTagTransforms.rewrite(content)` (same normalization as HXX1 lowering)
- Enforce raw-HEEx escape hatch policy:
  - If `content` contains raw markers (`<%`, `<%=` etc.) and not allowed, raise.
  - Allowed only under `@:allow_heex` (method/class) or `-D hxx_allow_raw_heex`.
- Return `ESigil("H", content, "")`.

VAR-BINDING LOWERING
- Extend `HeexStringReturnToSigilTransforms` to recognize `HeexTemplate.root(...)` as a template producer in returned-var patterns.

TESTS
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_inline_markup_basic
- Positive: test/snapshot/phoenix/heex_template_var_binding_root

VERIFICATION
- npm test

NOTES
- Canonical entrypoint is `phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1`; `phoenix.hxx.HXX2.root/1` remains as deprecated alias.
acceptance_criteria:
- phoenix.hxx.HeexTemplate.root/1 lowers to ~H
- Raw HEEx remains escape-hatch-only
- Var-binding conversions recognize HeexTemplate.root
- Existing HXX1 snapshots remain green

Template entrypoint detection includes root_ast, and suppression/producer recognition updated accordingly. Negative TSX guard snapshots remain green (tsx disallow string templates, allow_heex in tsx, untyped markers).

title: Tutorial: New Phoenix.Hx realtime chat (LiveView + Presence + PubSub)
description: Write a from-scratch tutorial and ship a reference example app that demonstrates a production-shaped realtime chat using Haxe-authored LiveView, Presence online users, and PubSub broadcasting. Keep output idiomatic and the dev loop robust (scaffold + watchers).
design: Chat architecture: Haxe-authored LiveView for UI; messages broadcast via Phoenix.PubSub; online users via Phoenix.Presence; optional OTP GenServer (Haxe) to keep last N messages in-memory for new joiners. Prefer server-only first; JS hooks optional. Use typed externs for Phoenix APIs; avoid __elixir__ in app code.
acceptance_criteria:
- Add new runnable example under examples/ (name TBD, e.g. examples/11-phoenix-chat/).
- Add tutorial doc (new page) with step-by-step instructions, code snippets, and a debugging section.
- Include at least: send message, broadcast to other sessions, show online count via Presence.
- Explicitly call out the typed abstractions being used (assigns/socket/params/types) and why they prevent common Phoenix/LiveView mistakes.
- Include a section showing the same feature written in a more functional Haxe style (small pure helpers, Result/Option, explicit rebinding) and how it maps cleanly to idiomatic Elixir.
- Add at least one Haxe-authored ExUnit test for the chat state module (if present).
- Add Playwright smoke spec exercising 2 sessions (message + presence) and include it in QA Sentinel Smoke.
- Ensure docs index + Phoenix new-app guide link to this tutorial (no duplicated long sections).
notes: Tutorial emphasis: explicitly teach how typed Phoenix abstractions (typed assigns/socket/params) reduce runtime errors, and show how to write Haxe in a functional style (data-in/data-out helpers, Result/Option flows, explicit rebinding) that compiles into clean idiomatic Elixir. This tutorial is Phoenix-first (portability is not the goal); link to the separate portability tutorial instead.

title: DevX: detach from external Haxe server after internal crash
description: When the default --wait port is occupied by an external Haxe server (often from another repo/session), we may attach and then get internal compiler crashes like: File "src/core/globals.ml" ... Assertion failed. Current restart path (stop/start) doesn't kill the external server, so we can loop. Detect internal failures on server compile when owns_server=false, detach, and start our own server on a fresh port for subsequent compiles.
notes: Default HaxeServer behavior no longer attaches to external --wait servers; opt-in via HAXE_SERVER_ALLOW_ATTACH=1. This avoids cross-project cache corruption (globals.ml assertion) and prevents stop/start loops from reattaching.

title: Phase 1.3: Create FinalUnderscorePrefixTransforms - move ALL underscore prefixing to final pass
description:
## Problem
`_this` is used after being set, which Elixir warns about:
```
warning: variable "_this" is unused (if the variable is not meant to be used, prefix it with an underscore)
```

The variable has underscore prefix but is still being used later in the code.

## Root Cause
Underscore prefix is applied in builders (too early), but usage is detected in transforms (too late).

Timeline problem:
1. Builder creates `_this` with underscore (assuming unused)
2. Later code uses `_this` 
3. Transform runs but underscore already applied
4. Elixir sees underscore-prefixed var being used = warning

## Solution
Move ALL underscore prefixing to a FINAL sentinel pass that runs after all other transforms.

## Files to Modify
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/builders/*.hx - Remove early underscore prefixing
- UPDATE: src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/FinalUnderscorePrefixTransforms.hx (may exist)

## Implementation
1. Remove underscore logic from all builders
2. Create/update final pass that:
   - Scans entire module for ALL variable definitions
   - Collects ALL variable usages across entire module
   - Only THEN applies underscore prefix to truly unused variables
3. Register as LAST pass in transformation pipeline

## Key Principle
Underscore prefix decision must happen AFTER all transformations that might add/remove usages.

## Dependencies
- Should run after: Phase 1.0A (this1 cleanup)
- Blocks: Phase 1.2 (removal pass needs correct usage data)

## Acceptance Criteria
- No "underscore variable used after set" warnings
- All truly unused variables get underscore prefix
- All used variables do NOT get underscore prefix
- npm test passes
- mix compile --force shows no underscore-usage warnings

## Effort: 2-3 hours | Impact: Fixes 2 warnings + prevents future issues
notes: Duplicate/outdated: Phase 1.3 underscore-prefixing work was already completed (see haxe.elixir-2co). Closing to keep backlog accurate.

title: Bind release tag, source commit, ZIP, and hosted asset with repair-only recovery
description: Replace selected-file and asset-name checks with one cryptographic release identity. Before tagging, fully verify the package and artifact record. title: Publish only the exact successfully tested main commit
description: Replace the privileged workflow_run release workflow, polling of separate workflows, and normal workflow_dispatch bypass with an explicit same-SHA job graph. Consolidate or call the required compiler, package, examples, dogfood, sentinel, and security gates from a push workflow so the publication job receives write authority only after all required jobs for github.sha succeed.

title: Build a reproducible Reflaxe.Elixir artifact without tracked release mutations

title: Replace generated release state with a policy-only SemVer core

Model initial-development behavior, explicit unsupported channels, and independent durable approval per stable major. The release configuration must load even when tracked development metadata is stale or malformed.
acceptance_criteria: The manifest contains no mutable current version, generated-file inventory, or posture blocks; fix, feat, and breaking commit sets are tested through the real analyzer; an unapproved 0.x breaking change derives the next minor; an explicitly approved graduation derives 1.0.0 only from a new graduation-authorizing change; stable breaking changes require the target major approval; multiple major approvals coexist; invalid SemVer, unknown majors, prerelease/build policy violations, and unsafe numeric components fail clearly; package metadata cannot prevent configuration loading.

title: Adopt the tested-commit SemVer reference release protocol
description: Replace the completed haxe.elixir.codex-m81 release-commit architecture with the simpler proven protocol from ../haxe.rust: CI tests source commit S, semantic-release derives version V from real tags and a small policy, a deterministic Reflaxe artifact is built from S with V injected only into staging, vV tags S, and GitHub publishes and verifies those exact bytes. Preserve the valid v0.14.x lineage while removing release-time tracked mutations, workflow_run trust ambiguity, and duplicated mutable release truth.
acceptance_criteria: Normal publication never changes tracked files or creates a release commit; exact version lineage comes from immutable reachable tags; pre-1.0 breaking commits remain minor until explicit per-major approval; the artifact is reproducible and bound to source SHA, tag, size, and SHA-256; only the exact successfully tested main SHA can publish; an existing-tag-only repair path completes partial GitHub publication without deriving a version or moving a tag; repository and host controls are documented and tested; a live release plus a subsequent no-op run records evidence.
notes: Audit evidence (2026-07-10): release.config.js currently loads mutable version/generation state, runs changelog and git plugins, writes tracked metadata/docs, pushes chore(release) commits, then tags those different commits. v0.14.23 points to release commit 9b256d7e, whose parent is source commit 212be207. .github/workflows/release.yml uses privileged workflow_run plus normal workflow_dispatch, polls other workflows, and does not encode an explicit same-repository push trust boundary. Package creation uses system find/cp/zip timestamps and ordering. Hosted verification downloads and structure-checks a same-name asset but does not bind it to the locally approved SHA-256. Immutable Releases are disabled and no repository rulesets are configured. The focused policy/generation/verification tests pass, showing internal consistency of the predecessor design rather than the target invariants.

title: Stdlib runtime: design Math special-float semantics before enabling upstream Math.unit.hx
description: Upstream Math.unit.hx expects Haxe/IEEE-style NaN and +/-Infinity behavior, but BEAM/Elixir raises for several operations before a float value exists. Local probes found 0 / 0 raises ArithmeticError, :math.sqrt(-1) raises, :math.log(0) raises, Float.parse("NaN"/"Infinity") returns :error, and direct IEEE NaN float decoding did not produce a usable Elixir float. Current std/Math.cross.hx defines NaN as 0.0 / 0.0 and approximates infinities as max finite floats, so enabling the upstream runtime spec fails and the semantics are not faithful. Before implementing, ask GPT 5.5 Pro with the full repo included because this touches Float arithmetic/comparison, Math.isNaN/isFinite, Math.min/max, Std.parseFloat, JSON output, and binary double encoding. Acceptance: choose and document the semantic model, implement it in source-of-truth Haxe/compiler runtime surfaces, add snapshots/runtime coverage, enable or adapt upstream Math.unit.hx with only justified target-specific skips, and pass npm run test:haxe-exunit-stdlib plus npm run guard:upstream-unitstd.
close_reason: GPT 5.5 Pro design accepted: use native finite numbers plus Reflaxe.Elixir.HaxeFloat tagged sentinels for NaN/+Infinity/-Infinity, with compiler-lowered Float-like operators and staged implementation. Decomposed into haxe.elixir-hm47.32.6 through haxe.elixir-hm47.32.12.

title: UX audit: generated API ergonomics consistency
description:
## Goal
Eliminate remaining UX friction where compiler-generated APIs still feel manual or inconsistent, now that `@:schema + @:changeset` no longer requires hand-written `extern changeset` declarations.

## Why this task
While fixing the changeset declaration DX, we found similar ergonomics issues that still increase cognitive overhead:
- legacy snapshot/examples still encode manual/verbose patterns and can regress docs back to old guidance
- mixed naming/qualification style (`Module.Type` vs direct type imports/constructors) makes snippets noisy
- no explicit regression coverage for "optional explicit declaration still works" compatibility path

## Scope
1. **Ecto snapshot cleanup**
- Modernize legacy schema/changeset snapshots that still require manual `extern` declarations for generated APIs.
- Keep one explicit compatibility test proving explicit declaration remains allowed.

2. **Snippet/API style normalization**
- Audit docs/examples for over-qualified type/constructor usage where unqualified usage is unambiguous.
- Standardize to concise style in user-facing snippets (import + direct type/constructor names).

3. **Regression guardrails**
- Add or adjust minimal snapshots so manual-boilerplate regression cannot return silently.
- Ensure docs/tests clearly separate:
  - generated API defaults (recommended)
  - explicit declarations (optional compatibility path)

## Out of scope
- New Ecto features beyond API ergonomics and docs consistency.
- Breaking changes to existing user code style requirements.

## Acceptance criteria
- Legacy docs/snippets no longer imply manual declaration is required for generated schema changesets.
- Snapshot coverage includes:
  - no-manual-declaration path (already added)
  - explicit-declaration compatibility path (kept and documented)
- User-facing docs consistently prefer concise, unqualified usage when no ambiguity exists.
- CI snapshot suites pass after intended updates.
close_reason: Implemented: docs normalization + compatibility regression coverage

title: Iterators: define canonical IMap representation + unwrap API
description:
# WHAT
Decide and document the canonical runtime representation for Elixir-target `haxe.Constraints.IMap` values.

# WHY
Iterator helpers and boundary code need a stable, non-brittle way to access the underlying key/value store without shape-sniffing (e.g. checking `:h`, `:map`, `:data`).

# HOW
- Pick one canonical representation strategy:
  - (A) Plain Elixir maps (`%{}`) everywhere (preferred if semantics allow), or
  - (B) A single wrapper shape with a single storage field (e.g. `:data`) plus `__reflaxe_class__` dispatch.
- Provide a single unwrapping API (e.g. `reflaxe.elixir.runtime.IMap.unwrap/1` or equivalent) as the *only* place that knows the representation.
- Add docs:
  - architecture note under `docs/05-architecture/` and hxdoc pointers.

# Acceptance
- A documented contract: “an `IMap` is represented as …” and “unwrap via …”.
- No app-specific name heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: See Acceptance in description.

# WHY

# HOW

  - plain `%{}`
  - canonical `IMap` representation chosen in task 1
  - `haxe.ds.BalancedTree` (via keys+get / unwrap contract)

- Runtime tests cover stateful iteration correctness.

title: Stdlib parity: canonical IMap runtime + iterators
description:
# Goal
Eliminate iterator/runtime and map-boundary gotchas by making Elixir-target `IMap` + iterator behavior **canonical, testable, and WAE-safe**.

This is the follow-up to a CI-unblocker where iterator stubs were promoted to minimal runtime modules to satisfy `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`. The long-term goal is to move that logic out of transformer overrides and into a single, well-defined stdlib/runtime layer.

# Motivation
- CI WAE shards failed when generated stdlib called `ArrayIterator.new/1` / `MapKeyValueIterator.new/1` but the modules were docs-only stubs.
- Current runtime unwrapping for `IMap` is implemented via *shape sniffing* (checking for `:h`, `:map`, `:data`), which is brittle unless backed by an explicit runtime representation contract.
- We want “use Haxe Map everywhere” with predictable behavior and idiomatic Elixir output, and we want the server (Elixir) and client (genes/JS) story to remain coherent.

# Current state
- Iterator runtime exists as an AST override in `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/StdHaxeRuntimeOverrideTransforms.hx` (`ArrayIterator` + `MapKeyValueIterator`).
- The implementation preserves Haxe's stateful iterator calling convention by storing index state in the process dictionary keyed by a unique ref.
- Map unwrapping is currently shape-based.

# Proposed direction (single source of truth)
1) Define and enforce a **canonical Elixir representation for Elixir-target `IMap`** (one storage field or one runtime helper API).
2) Implement iterator modules as real Elixir-target stdlib/runtime modules (not emitted by transformer overrides), keeping the exact upstream Haxe API surface.
3) Keep transformer overrides only as a temporary safety net until the stdlib implementations are complete and covered by runtime tests.

# Non-goals
- Do not rewrite the entire compiler to an immutable iterator protocol in this epic (separate research).
- Do not introduce `Dynamic` public surfaces to paper over mismatches.

# Acceptance criteria
- A documented canonical `IMap` representation/unwrap contract (docs + hxdoc).
- `haxe.iterators.ArrayIterator` and `haxe.iterators.MapKeyValueIterator` have real Elixir-target implementations (stdlib/runtime) with `new/arity`, `hasNext/has_next`, and `next/1` semantics preserved.
- Remove (or greatly narrow) iterator logic from `StdHaxeRuntimeOverrideTransforms` without regressing WAE.
- Add runtime tests proving iterator semantics and key/value iteration across:
  - plain Elixir maps (`%{}`)
  - Haxe map-backed wrappers (whatever canonical form we pick)
  - `haxe.ds.BalancedTree` map impl
- CI `Examples (Elixir WAE)` remains green.

# References
- CI-unblocker hxdoc: `src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/transformers/StdHaxeRuntimeOverrideTransforms.hx`
- WAE harness: `scripts/test-examples-elixir.sh`

title: Stdlib parity roadmap (Haxe 4.3.x baseline)
description:
# Goal
Close the Elixir-target stdlib parity gap (Haxe 4.3.x baseline) so that normal Haxe code compiles and runs correctly on BEAM, while generated Elixir stays idiomatic.

This epic is about compatibility and correctness first, then idiomaticity/optimizations where semantics allow.

# Single source of truth
Module-level audit artifacts live in the repo and must stay current:
- `docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.json`
- `docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.md`
- Regeneration script: `scripts/stdlib-parity-report.sh`

Regenerate locally:
```bash
export HAXE_ELIXIR_REFERENCE=/path/to/haxe.compilerdev.reference
scripts/stdlib-parity-report.sh --json > docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.json
scripts/stdlib-parity-report.sh --markdown > docs/08-roadmap/stdlib-parity/gap-report.md
```

# Current baseline (June 2026)
Latest counts (reference vs local std modules present):
- Reference std modules: **204**
- Local std modules present: **98** (candidates scanned: 101)
- Intersection (local provides): **89**
- Missing locally (reference-only): **115**
- Local-only: **9**

Top-level modules missing locally (5):
- `Any`, `Class`, `Enum`, `EnumValue`, `StdTypes`

Note: The report counts compiler-emitted runtime overrides as present where applicable.

# Scope / Definition of parity
We need an explicit policy per module:

1) **Upstream fallback OK**
- Module compiles and behaves correctly on BEAM without overrides.
- Add focused snapshots/runtime tests for high-traffic modules.

2) **Needs Elixir override / BEAM mapping**
- Module relies on host APIs (`sys.*`), platform-specific assumptions, or produces invalid/non-idiomatic Elixir.
- Implement as `std/**/*.cross.hx` or target-gated `std/_std/**` when it is a stable API mapping.
- Prefer AST transforms only when the fix is shape-driven and not an API override.

3) **Explicitly unsupported (documented + fail fast)**
- Non-portable semantics that cannot be reproduced reasonably on BEAM.
- Must fail with actionable errors and docs; no silent stubs.

# Plan (phased)
Phase 0 — Audit + guardrails
- Keep `gap-report.*` current.
- Maintain/expand `docs/04-api-reference/STDLIB_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md` with clear supported/unsupported rationale.

Phase 1 — `sys.*` core
- `sys.io.Process` strategy is implemented.
- `sys.net.*`, `sys.thread.*`, `sys.ssl.*`, and `sys.Http` strategy/mappings are documented or implemented where appropriate.
- Remaining `sys.db.*` should be documented unsupported or mapped intentionally if a downstream library needs it.

Phase 2 — High-impact pure std modules
- Done: `Xml`, `UnicodeString`, `UInt`, `haxe.CallStack`, core map/iterator surfaces, bytes/io foundations, `haxe.Http` / `sys.Http`, and the `haxe.Serializer` / `haxe.Unserializer` portable data subset.
- Next candidates: `haxe.Template`, remaining `haxe.io.*` utilities, and Serializer/Unserializer class/enum/custom expansion if downstream libraries need it.

# Deliverables
- Gap report + support matrix docs are authoritative and easy to regenerate.
- Each implemented module has snapshot coverage and runtime tests where semantics matter.

# Acceptance criteria
- A documented, enforced policy for stdlib parity (supported vs needs-override vs unsupported).
- High-impact surfaces have either a BEAM mapping implementation or explicit unsupported docs.
- No public-surface `Dynamic` introduced as a workaround beyond canonical Haxe stdlib APIs that require `Dynamic`.
- Todo-app sentinel and WAE example checks remain part of verification for behavior-affecting stdlib work.

# Tracking
- Roadmap tasks are children of this epic.
- Support matrix pointer: `docs/04-api-reference/STDLIB_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md`.
notes: Runtime conformance track: snapshots validate generated Elixir shape; upstream Haxe unitstd specs should be reused through the Haxe→ExUnit lane to validate stdlib runtime behavior on BEAM for supported/overridden modules.
close_reason: All child tasks are complete and the stdlib parity roadmap epic is eligible for close.

title: HXX: make heexAST the primary lint source

## What
Ensure HXX linting always prefers `metadata.heexAST` and only uses string fallback when explicitly enabled.

## Why
TSX-level feedback relies on AST stability. String scanning is fragile and causes missed/false diagnostics.

## How
- Audit `HeexAssignsTypeLinterTransforms` fallback paths.
- Gate fallback behind a define (e.g. `-D hxx_allow_string_fallback`) and default it off when AST spans exist.
- Add negative snapshots that would previously only fail in string mode.

## Acceptance
- Snapshots stable (or updated with a justification for any intentional behavior change).
- Todo-app templates still lint and compile.

title: HXX: add opt-in strict unknown HTML tag checking
description:
## What
Add `-D hxx_strict_html` that errors on unknown HTML tags unless registered/whitelisted.

## Acceptance

title: TSX-level HXX typing + extensibility
description:
# TSX-level HXX typing + extensibility

## Goal
Make HXX/HEEx authoring feel as close as possible to TSX:
- Strong, actionable compile-time feedback for tags/attrs/slots/events/hooks.
- Clear, documented escape hatches (raw HEEx strings / untyped tags) without punishing early adopters.
- A stable “vocab” that apps can extend (custom tags/components/hooks/events) without patching compiler internals.

## Scope
- Compiler-side linting/type checks: `HeexAssignsTypeLinterTransforms` and related passes.
- Registries in stdlib: HTML tags/attrs, dot-components, hooks/events.
- Docs + app-template recommendations (strict flags, registries, best practices).
- Optional IDE tooling index (JSON) generated from the same registries.

## Non-goals (for now)
- Haxe 5 support work.
- Full editor integration (we’ll emit an index; IDE plugins can come later).

## Acceptance Criteria
- New strict modes are opt-in, documented, and covered by snapshot tests.
- Default behavior remains permissive for unknown/custom tags.
- Prefer AST metadata (`metadata.heexAST`) over string scanning.

title: Generate typed LiveView hook protocol bindings
description: Adopt and implement PhoenixHx typed LiveView event protocols as an opt-in framework macro layer. Developers declare a shared Haxe enum protocol once; PhoenixHx generates event names, target-native JS hook push helpers, target-native Elixir/JS payload encode/decode helpers, and server LiveView dispatch helpers. LiveViews keep normal Phoenix-shaped handleEvent(event, params, socket) and explicitly call the generated dispatcher. No metadata means no behavior change. WirePayload/WireCodec remain low-level manual/open-boundary tools, not the default generated protocol path.
design:
Adopt protocol-first, explicit-dispatch, handler-validated v1. Prefer @:liveEventProtocol on a shared enum and @:liveEvents(ProtocolEnum) on the LiveView, with derived names by default and string overrides for interop. Do not auto-wrap or replace handleEvent in v1. Do not infer protocols from arbitrary handleEvent bodies. Defer typed replies and custom runtime event systems. Use docs/08-roadmap/phoenixhx-live-event-protocols.md as the source of truth.

Implementation note from Tink Web: build a normalized macro model first (LiveEventCollection, LiveEventSignature, LiveEventPayload, LiveEventField), then generate browser push helpers and server dispatch helpers from that same model. Borrow Tink Web's declaration -> model -> client/server generation pattern, but not its HTTP router complexity, handler-body inference, or unstable generated counters.
acceptance_criteria:
A shared enum protocol such as ProfileHookEvent generates a companion such as ProfileHookEvents with typed encode/decode and per-event JS push helpers.
The macro implementation first normalizes protocol declarations into a deterministic shared model used by both generated client helpers and generated server dispatch helpers.
ProfileLive can opt in with @:liveEvents(ProfileHookEvent), gets a derived dispatchProfileHookEvent helper, and keeps an explicit dispatch-first handleEvent fallback.
Generated built-in payload encoders/decoders use target-native JS object and Elixir map operations, not WirePayload/WireCodec runtime helper plumbing; generated Elixir/JS is snapshot-tested and reviewable.
Known events with malformed payloads are consumed safely instead of falling through as unknown events.
Diagnostics cover duplicate event names, unsupported Dynamic/map payloads, duplicate wire keys, missing/wrong handlers, and dispatcher-call validation; dispatcher-call validation is warning by default and strict-mode error under a define.
Todo-app migrates clipboard_copied and ping from manual HookEvents to generated protocol helpers while direct Phoenix handleEvent remains documented as the baseline alternative.
Validation includes Haxe client/server builds, snapshots/diagnostics, todo-app ExUnit coverage, and async QA sentinel with Playwright for clipboard flash and ping no-op behavior.

title: Add RailsHx-inspired PhoenixHx todo learning example
description:
PLAN_REF: plans/active/railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo-example.md

FILES
- New example root: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/
- Example docs: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/README.md and examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/docs/RAILSHX_TO_PHOENIXHX.md
- Example Haxe app: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/src_haxe/**
- Example assets/client: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/assets/**, build-client.hxml, package.json if needed
- Example tests: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/src_haxe/test/** and examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/e2e/**
- Build/config: examples/17-railshx-to-phoenixhx-todo/build.hxml, build-tests.hxml, build-client.hxml, mix.exs, config/*.exs
- QA registry: examples/qa-manifest.json
- Examples index/docs links: examples/README.md and any canonical docs index that lists numbered examples
- Source reference only, do not modify unless explicitly required: https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails

WHAT
Create a didactic Phoenix/Reflaxe.Elixir example that ports the RailsHx todo app UX from https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails/ while using Phoenix-native architecture. The output should teach how the same Haxe-authored product surface maps differently to Rails and Phoenix: RailsHx uses ActiveRecord, ActionController, HHX-to-ERB, Turbo Streams, Devise, and Rails route helpers; PhoenixHx should use Ecto, contexts, LiveView, inline HXX function components, PubSub/LiveView updates, session/on_mount auth, and Phoenix routes.

USER-FACING UX CONTRACT
- Preserve the RailsHx visual hierarchy and interaction vocabulary where practical: authenticated app chrome/top bar, guest sign-in/demo access, todo composer, summary/empty state, todo cards/list, completion/toggle/delete flows, user attribution, status/flash polish, and progressive focus/scroll niceties.
- Include chat and user-management panels only if they fit cleanly after the todo/auth slice. If they are too broad, create follow-up child tasks for them instead of overloading the first implementation.
- The app should feel like the RailsHx sample viewed through Phoenix conventions, not like a clone of the existing examples/todo-app product surface.

ALGORITHM / IMPLEMENTATION PLAN
1. Inventory RailsHx source
   - Read https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails/README.md, models, controllers, views, shared/TodoHooks.hx, client/TodoClient.hx, and e2e/todoapp.spec.ts.
   - Write the UX contract into the new README before implementation drifts.

2. Scaffold a numbered Phoenix example
   - Use existing local Phoenix example patterns, preferring compact shapes from examples/13-elixir-first-liveview or examples/15-phoenix-chat-haxe-first over copying the heavyweight examples/todo-app wholesale.
   - Keep Phoenix project files idiomatic: mix.exs/config/router/assets remain Phoenix-shaped; Haxe owns app/domain/UI/test code where the example is trying to teach Haxe authoring.

3. Port Rails domain to Ecto/Phoenix boundaries
   - Todo/User required; ChatMessage optional follow-up unless implemented within the same bounded scope.
   - Model fields and validations become Ecto schema + changeset + context functions.
   - Rails strong params become context-layer changeset casting/validation. Do not create a fake strong-params API.
   - Owner/user fields must be server-controlled, matching the RailsHx security intent.

4. Port routes/auth/session edges
   - Implement Phoenix routes for home/todos and demo guest sign-in/logout.
   - Use Phoenix session/controller/on_mount conventions instead of Devise/Warden compatibility facades.
   - Document where a real production auth library would replace the demo session flow.

5. Port UI to LiveView and inline HXX
   - Use inline HXX/TSX authoring. Do not use hxx('...') / HXX.hxx('...') except for explicit legacy coverage, which this task is not.
   - Extract function components for top bar, composer, summary, todo list/card, and optional side panels.
   - Use LiveView events for create/toggle/delete and PubSub/handle_info where cross-session updates are shown.
   - Use CSS/assets adapted from the RailsHx sample as a visual reference, while keeping Phoenix asset conventions.

6. Port progressive client behavior
   - Create typed shared hook constants equivalent to RailsHx shared/TodoHooks.hx.
   - Compile Haxe client hooks through Genes if the example has browser-only behavior.
   - Keep client code progressive. It may handle autofocus, scroll preservation, small status flashes, or key handling; it must not duplicate server-rendered HTML.

7. Tests and QA
   - Add Haxe-authored ExUnit tests for route/session/LiveView CRUD flows.
   - Add a thin Playwright smoke based on the RailsHx spec and selectors.
   - Register the example in examples/qa-manifest.json with meaningful runtime/E2E coverage or an explicit compile-only rationale for any intentionally uncovered layer.
   - Update example generated output/snapshots if this repo tracks generated output for the new example.

8. Documentation
   - README must link to https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails/ and explain how to run and validate the PhoenixHx port.
   - Add docs/RAILSHX_TO_PHOENIXHX.md with a concrete crosswalk: ActiveRecord -> Ecto, ActionController -> LiveView/controller edges, strong params -> changeset, HHX partial -> inline HXX component, Turbo Streams -> LiveView/PubSub, Devise -> session/on_mount auth, Rails routes -> Phoenix routes, Rails tests -> Haxe-authored ExUnit/Playwright.
   - Include a future-tooling section separating deterministic conversion inventory from human decisions and possible later Haxe abstractions.

FAILURE MODES / GAPS TO SURFACE
- If Phoenix route helper/verified route typing is too weak, use a small example-local wrapper and document the gap; do not invent non-existent Phoenix APIs.
- If typed function component/local ergonomics are missing compared to RailsHx HHX partials, document the gap and create a follow-up task instead of widening types to Dynamic.
- If chat/user-management make the task too broad, split them into child tasks after the todo/auth slice.
- If the app needs compiler/framework surface changes, stop and create separate narrowly scoped tasks with regression coverage.
- Do not commit generated files containing machine-local absolute paths.

TESTS
- Haxe compile for the new example via its build.hxml/build-tests.hxml.
- Haxe-authored ExUnit tests for create/toggle/delete/session/empty-state flows.
- Playwright smoke for home/demo sign-in/todo composer/list/toggle/delete using resilient selectors.
- examples/qa-manifest.json guarded by npm run guard:examples-qa.
- Example compile/output/strict/runtime suites updated as appropriate.

VERIFICATION
- npm run guard:examples-qa
- npm run test:examples
- npm run test:examples-output
- npm run test:examples-elixir
- npm run test:examples-runtime
- New example runtime smoke via scripts/qa-sentinel.sh with --async and --deadline if a Phoenix server is booted.
- For any todo-app-adjacent runtime verification, use the QA sentinel only; never run mix phx.server in the foreground.

ROLLOUT
- Add as a new numbered example; do not replace examples/todo-app.
- Keep the example self-contained and educational.
- Commit docs, source, tests, manifest updates, and intended generated-output changes together.
- Push after local verification, then confirm latest main CI is green before starting the next task.
acceptance_criteria: New numbered Phoenix example preserves the RailsHx todo UX; README and conversion crosswalk link to https://github.com/fullofcaffeine/reflaxe.ruby/tree/main/examples/todoapp_rails; example is registered in examples/qa-manifest.json with compile/runtime/E2E coverage; Haxe-authored ExUnit and Playwright smoke cover the main flows; required example test commands pass under bounded runners.

title: Stateful expression hoisting: local ++/-- inside ExUnit assertions must rebind outer variable
description: While adding HaxeFloat Stage 2 runtime coverage, a direct Assert.equals(..., ++counter) / Assert.equals(..., counter++) shape compiled into an ExUnit assertion expression where the local rebind stayed inside the assertion/macro expression and did not update the outer counter. This is the same family as same-scope stateful expression hoisting, but for local increment/decrement rather than receiver effects.
acceptance_criteria: Add focused Haxe-authored ExUnit/runtime coverage for local postfix and prefix increments inside assertion arguments and other value positions. Lower the stateful increment into a same-scope prelude so the outer local is rebound before ExUnit/assertion/IIFE transforms can isolate it. Keep ordinary statement and assignment-position increments passing.
close_reason: Fixed local ++/-- same-scope rebinding by lowering local mutation through receiver-effect plans, preserving prefix/postfix values in assertions and value expressions; updated reducer accumulator threading for late/nested mutation shapes. Verified guard:hx-format, test:haxe-exunit-stdlib, and test:quick.

title: Compiler: fix Ecto Changeset abstract method lowering for chains and reassignments

Fix the root AST/inline lowering so Changeset methods consistently emit and return the intended Ecto.Changeset call results.
acceptance_criteria: Add focused regressions for fluent chain, single-method return, and same-variable reassignment shapes using Changeset.validateRequired/validateLength/validateInclusion/validateExclusion. Generated Elixir must retain each Ecto.Changeset call and return the final call result. Do not repair by post-processing generated strings; fix the compiler/stdlib lowering root cause.
close_reason: Fixed by 663c9e37d (Fix Ecto changeset validation lowering); latest main CI, examples, QA sentinel, dogfood, CodeQL, and release workflows are green.

title: IMap design: native %{}-backed haxe.ds.Map surface
description:
# WHAT
Decide whether the Elixir target should implement the `haxe.ds.*Map` family as a thin, native `%{}` wrapper where `get/set/exists/remove/keys/iterator` compile to `Map.get/3`, `Map.put/3`, etc.

# WHY
Boundary values (Phoenix params, Presence lists, JSON payloads) are frequently plain Elixir maps. When Haxe code expects a `Map<K,V>` API, we either:
- convert at the boundary (allocations + less idiomatic), or
- make the Elixir target’s Map implementation *be* a native map (best DevX, but requires careful parity + macro safety).

# OPTIONS
A) Boundary conversion only
- Keep `haxe.ds.*Map` as-is (tree-backed / wrapper structs).
- Convert boundary `%{}` to Haxe Map at decode boundaries.

B) Native map-backed `haxe.ds.*Map` (Elixir-target implementation)
- `new Map()` produces a `%{}` (or a tiny wrapper) and methods compile to `Map.*` calls.
- Great DX at client/server boundaries; less “gotcha” behavior.
- Needs careful work for:
  - macro/eval safety (dual-mode stubs)
  - iteration semantics / stable ordering expectations
  - `IMap` typing surface compatibility

# ACCEPTANCE
- Record a decision with explicit tradeoffs and impact on:
  - WAE
  - macro/eval
  - performance
  - portability to non-Elixir targets
- If (B) is selected, spin up an implementation plan under the stdlib parity epic with runtime behavior tests.
acceptance_criteria: - Decision recorded with pros/cons and chosen direction\n- If chosen, follow-up tasks created for implementation + tests
close_reason: Chose staged native-map backing for Elixir built-in Haxe map surfaces: Map/StringMap/IntMap use native %{ } and Map.* lowering, while ObjectMap identity semantics and Map abstract conversion/copy behavior remain explicit follow-up work. Documented WAE, macro/eval, performance, and portability tradeoffs; created follow-ups haxe.elixir-hm47.23.7, haxe.elixir-hm47.23.8, and haxe.elixir-hm47.23.9.

title: Optimize safe in-place array mutation loops → Enum.map
description:
# Goal
Improve codegen for user-written “imperative array mutation loops” by rewriting proven-safe patterns into `Enum.map/2` (or `Enum.with_index/1 |> Enum.map/2`) so output is both idiomatic and efficient.

# Problem
Today, a loop like:

```haxe
var i = 0;
while (i < array.length) {
  array[i] = transform(array[i]);
  i++;
}
```

**compiles correctly**, but because `Array` is represented as an immutable list for the Elixir target, indexed updates require rebuilding the list. In a loop this can become O(n²) and the generated Elixir is less idiomatic.

We already generate optimal code for *Haxe-desugared* `array.map/filter` patterns, but not for arbitrary user-authored while loops.

# Desired behavior
When the compiler can prove the loop is a pure “map-in-place” (or map-with-index) and the counter is not semantically observed afterward, rewrite to:

- `array = Enum.map(array, fn item -> ... end)`
- or `array = Enum.with_index(array) |> Enum.map(fn {item, i} -> ... end)` when index is used in the RHS.

# Safety constraints
Only rewrite when all of the following hold:
- loop condition is a simple bound over `i` vs `array.length`
- body has exactly one array element update and one counter increment (no early returns, break/continue, or additional mutations)
- the counter’s post-loop value is not observed (either it’s a synthetic `_g*` var or provably unused after the loop within the containing block)
- array reference is stable (local or a stable captured value)

# Tests
Add a focused snapshot under `test/snapshot/core/` that:
- compiles the imperative loop form
- validates the output is rewritten to Enum.map/with_index
- includes a “do not rewrite” negative/adjacent case (e.g. i used after loop)
close_reason: Implemented safe map-in-place array loop lowering to Enum.map/Enum.with_index with block-level counter-use guard, docs, focused snapshot, full chunks, examples WAE, mix-fast, and todo-app Playwright sentinel.

comments.author: fullofcaffeine
comments.text: Discovery is currently broken: RepoDiscovery collects type paths but never calls Context.getType, and ElixirCompiler.filterTypes returns early without appending discovered modules. This means unreferenced @:repo/@:presence/@:endpoint/@:router/@:phoenixWeb modules may never be typed/emitted.\n\nPlan: rewrite RepoDiscovery to scan project classpaths for .hx files containing relevant metadata tokens, parse Haxe package+class, call Context.getType(haxePath) to force typing, and keep RepoEnumerator @:keep so DCE cannot drop them. Update comments in CompilerInit/ElixirCompiler to reflect the new behavior and add regression coverage (snapshot or small fixture) to ensure an unreferenced @:repo extern still emits a Repo module.

comments.author: fullofcaffeine
comments.text:
Done: fast_boot no longer skips correctness-critical module discovery/keeping.

- Added AnnotatedModuleEnumerator to mark framework-annotated modules (e.g. @:repo, @:presence, @:endpoint, @:router, @:supervisor, etc.) as @:keep/@:used so Haxe DCE can’t drop them when referenced only indirectly (supervision trees / ModuleRef("...")).
- Updated CompilerInit.Start() to always enable discovery + keep macros; RepoDiscovery now uses a temp-file cache under fast_boot to avoid repeated project-wide scans.
- Added snapshot coverage: test/snapshot/phoenix/presence_discovery (unreferenced @:presence module must still be emitted under -dce full).
- Removed now-unnecessary app-level @:keep from todo-app Presence (examples/todo-app/src_haxe/server/presence/TodoPresence.hx).

title: Phase 1.0B: Architectural fix in TypedQueryLambda.hx - eliminate this1 at macro source
description:
## Problem
TypedQuery macros generate ERaw nodes via `__elixir__()` which contain `this1` sentinel patterns that AST transforms cannot see or clean up.

## Root Cause
TypedQueryLambda.hx line 35:
```haxe
macro new ecto.TypedQuery.TypedQuery(untyped __elixir__($v{code}, $ethis, $right));
```

This generates code like:
```elixir
(fn ->
  this1 = nil
  this1 = Ecto.Query.from(t in Todo, [])
  this1
end).()
```

The `this1` is Haxe's internal pattern for abstract method chaining return values.

## Solution: Generate Structured AST
Instead of `__elixir__()` -> ERaw, TypedQuery should generate structured AST:

Option 1: Use ERemoteCall instead of __elixir__()
```haxe
return ERemoteCall(EAtom("Ecto.Query"), "where", [
    buildQueryAst(thisExpr),
    lambdaBinding,
    buildConditionAst(right)
]);
```

Option 2: Restructure to avoid this1 entirely
Generate: Ecto.Query.where(query, [t], condition) without intermediate this1 sentinel

## Files to Modify
- src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/TypedQueryLambda.hx - Restructure macro to avoid this1

## Dependencies
- Depends on: Phase 1.0A (string cleanup provides immediate relief while this is developed)
- Blocks: Final 1.0 release (this is the proper long-term solution)

## Acceptance Criteria
- TypedQuery.where() generates clean Ecto.Query.where() calls
- No this1 pattern in generated TypedQuery code
- EFnTempChainSimplifyTransforms can see and process all query AST
- npm test passes
- All existing TypedQuery tests continue to work

## Effort: 4-6 hours | Impact: Eliminates root cause, prevents future this1 issues
notes: Reopened (was closed by mistake; pending work + verification).

title: Phase 1.0A: this1 string-level cleanup in ElixirASTPrinter.hx
description:
## Problem
Generated Elixir code contains unused `this1` variable warnings in 3 files:
- todo_live.ex (load_todos function)
- user_changeset.ex
- user_controller.ex

## Root Cause Analysis (Investigation Complete)
1. TypedQuery macros use `__elixir__()` for query generation
2. `__elixir__()` creates ERaw nodes - opaque strings in AST
3. Haxe generates `this1` sentinel for abstract method chaining: `var this1 = nil; this1 = expr; this1`
4. AST transforms can't see inside ERaw - EFnTempChainSimplifyTransforms is blind to it
5. When ERaw is multi-line, `sanitizeArgPrinted()` wraps in string-level IIFE
6. Cleanup passes already ran on AST, so they never see these string-level IIFEs

## Example of Problematic Generated Code
```elixir
defp load_todos(_user_id) do
    TodoApp.Repo.all((fn ->
      query = Ecto.Query.where((fn -> query = Ecto.Query.from(t in TodoApp.Todo, [])
      this1 = nil      # <-- WARNING: unused
      this1 = query
      this1 end).(), [t], t.user_id == ^(user_id))
      this1 = nil      # <-- WARNING: unused
      this1 = query
      this1
    end).())
end
```

## Solution: String-Level Cleanup (Quick Win)
Add post-processing cleanup in ElixirASTPrinter.hx after IIFE wrapping.

## Files to Modify
- src/reflaxe/elixir/ast/ElixirASTPrinter.hx - Add string cleanup in sanitizeArgPrinted() or new helper

## Acceptance Criteria
- No this1 warnings in todo_live.ex, user_changeset.ex, user_controller.ex
- npm test passes
- mix compile --force shows no this1 warnings

## Effort: 2-3 hours | Impact: Fixes ~6 warnings immediately

title: Perf: measure todo-app watch cycle time (mix haxe.watch)
description:
# WHAT
Add a bounded measurement of edit→rebuild latency when using `mix haxe.watch` / the todo-app watcher.

# WHY
The biggest DevX pain is often the incremental “watch” cycle, not the cold compile. We need a baseline to know what “good” looks like and to detect major regressions.

# HOW
- Create a small script that:
  - starts the watcher in the background (bounded; auto-terminates)
  - touches a single representative Haxe file in the todo-app (or a generated copy) to trigger rebuild
  - measures time until “compile done” signal appears in logs
  - repeats N times and outputs p50/p95
- Keep it non-gating by default; store results as JSON.

# Acceptance
- Running the script locally prints a short summary and writes a JSON artifact.
- The script is bounded (uses `scripts/with-timeout.sh`) and leaves no background processes.
acceptance_criteria: - Script reports watch cycle latency distribution (p50/p95)\n- Output includes environment + phases\n- Docs explain how to run locally

title: Spike: formalize portable|metal contract for reflaxe.elixir while preserving elixir-first ergonomics
description:
## Why
Current Elixir model is strong architecturally, but `portable vs elixir-first` is mostly documented as authoring guidance. We need an explicit profile contract aligned with family semantics and CI gates.

## Inputs
- Family/canonical references from Go:
  - `../haxe.go/docs/portable-canonical-contract.md`
  - `../haxe.go/docs/profiles.md`
  - `../haxe.go/docs/phase2-roadmap.md`
- Elixir references:
  - `docs/02-user-guide/AUTHORING_STYLES_PORTABLE_VS_ELIXIR_FIRST.md`
  - `src/reflaxe/elixir/CompilerInit.hx`
  - `src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/StrictModeEnforcer.hx`
  - `src/reflaxe/elixir/macros/BoundaryEnforcer.hx`

## Spike Scope
1. Define how to express Elixir `portable|metal` as compiler contract (not replacing authoring docs).
2. Specify profile presets over orthogonal axes:
   - strictness policy
   - runtime/support-module policy
   - interop boundary policy
3. Propose migration plan with low disruption:
   - optional fallback/warn mode for metal migration
   - contract tests for portable semantic subset
   - docs consolidation path

## Deliverables
- Architecture spike doc with:
  - current vs target model
  - compatibility risks
  - implementation phases
  - CI test-matrix changes
- Follow-up beads tasks (prioritized; default low priority unless blockers).

## Future Follow-up Trigger
After `haxe.go` selective runtime + metal fallback lands, run a new GPT-5.2 Pro comparative spike across Go/Rust/Elixir/hxhx using updated code and docs to finalize family spec.
close_reason: Architecture spike complete: documented the Reflaxe.Elixir authoring-profile contract in docs/05-architecture/AUTHORING_PROFILE_CONTRACT.md, linked it from user and architecture docs, clarified that portable and Elixir-first are authoring profiles rather than backend switches, scoped metal to local escape hatches, captured compatibility risks/CI axes/implementation phases, and created follow-up haxe.elixir-960 for optional diagnostic-only profile linting.
